chains.title: TCF7L2 binding at an 8q24 enhancer regulates MYC

links.claim: TCF7L2 occupies this element in HCT116. The hypothesis is that the alt C allele binds TCF7L2 more strongly than the ref T allele. No QBiC-SELEX model for TCF7L2 was supplied and no allele-specific binding data are given, so the direction is an untested inference, not direct evidence.
The variant lies in an active proximal enhancer-like cCRE, EH38E3858447, with DNase and H3K27ac signal consistent with a regulatory element.

The proposed target is MYC, 334.2 kb upstream. MYC is a plausible 8q24/CRC gene, but there is no direct enhancer-promoter evidence supplied; MYC knockout has a strong growth effect in HCT116 but MYC is common-essential, so this does not establish enhancer specificity.
HCT116 is the relevant colorectal cancer cell line because TCF7L2 occupancy at this element and TCF7L2 expression are observed there.

Altered TCF7L2-dependent enhancer activity at 8q24 could affect MYC expression and colorectal cancer biology, but the supplied evidence is general CRC literature rather than variant-specific mechanism.

predictions: Allele-specific TCF7L2 ChIP or EMSA shows stronger binding to the C allele than the T allele.
CRISPR editing of the variant or deletion of EH38E3858447 changes MYC expression in HCT116.
TCF7L2 depletion reduces MYC expression and colorectal cancer cell growth.
falsified_if: allele-specific TCF7L2 ChIP or reporter assays show no difference between T and C
TCF7L2 knockdown or enhancer deletion does not change MYC in HCT116
the variant is shown to be in complete linkage with another causal variant that explains the signal

chains.title: Null: no TF-mediated effect of this variant
predictions: No allele-specific TF binding or enhancer activity difference at chr8:127401265 T>C.
Any disease association is explained by a linked variant, 8q24 context, or no allelic effect at this base.
falsified_if: allele-specific reporter or TF ChIP assays show no reproducible T/C effect at this base
a linked causal variant is excluded and this variant is shown to directly alter TF binding and gene expression

chains.title: SP1 binding at the same enhancer regulates POU5F1B

links.claim: SP1 occupies this element in HCT116. The hypothesis is that the alt C allele binds SP1 more strongly than the ref T allele. No QBiC-SELEX model for SP1 was supplied and no allele-specific binding data are given, so the direction is an untested inference.
The variant lies in the active pELS EH38E3858447, a plausible SP1-responsive enhancer.

POU5F1B is 79.1 kb away and is the best L2G gene in the supplied credible sets, but those credible sets are for PSA and urinary incontinence, not colorectal cancer; no GTEx eQTL for this SNP was supplied.
HCT116 is the matching colorectal cancer cell line with SP1 occupancy at the element and SP1 expression.
POU5F1B has literature support in colorectal cancer, but the supplied evidence does not establish a variant-specific SP1-POU5F1B disease mechanism.

predictions: Allele-specific SP1 binding is higher on the C allele.
SP1 knockdown reduces POU5F1B expression in HCT116.
The enhancer contacts the POU5F1B promoter in HCT116.
falsified_if: SP1 ChIP or reporter assays show no allele-specific effect
SP1 depletion does not affect POU5F1B expression in HCT116
POU5F1B is not expressed or not regulated from this enhancer in colorectal cells

grades_v0.reason: Occupancy evidence is supported for HCT116 (E04), but the claim that the 'alt C allele is proposed to bind TCF7L2 more strongly' is a directional prediction unsupported by QBiC-SELEX or allele-specific binding assays.
E01 and E03 confirm the variant lies within an active proximal enhancer-like cCRE (pELS) element (EH38E3858447) with DNase and H3K27ac signal.

E02 provides proximity data for MYC (334.2 kb upstream), and E18 provides general CRC context, but there is no evidence of a direct regulatory interaction or linkage between this specific enhancer and MYC.
E04 and E05 confirm TCF7L2 occupancy and expression specifically in the HCT116 cell line.
E18 only provides general literature hits regarding TCF7L2 and CRC, not specific evidence linking altered TCF7L2 activity at this locus to altered MYC and subsequent CRC biology.

Occupancy evidence is supported in HCT116 (E04), but the claim regarding the directional effect ('alt C allele is proposed to bind SP1 more strongly') is a prediction lacking QBiC-SELEX or allele-specific binding data.
E03 supports the element being an active pELS, which is a plausible binding site for an SP1-responsive enhancer.
E02 places POU5F1B (79.1 kb) in close proximity, and E16 provides strong L2G evidence identifying POU5F1B as the best candidate gene for the variant.
E04 and E06 confirm SP1 occupancy and expression specifically in the HCT116 cell line.
While POU5F1B has general literature hits in CRC (E18), the provided evidence does not establish a mechanistic link demonstrating that this specific variant/SP1 pathway affects the cancer phenotype.
The crucial evidence of CTCF occupancy within the required cell type (HCT116) is absent. E07 only reports CTCF binding in other biosamples (e.g., HepG2, A549).
E03 supports the element being a pELS with a high CTCF z-score (z=5.5), which is consistent with an insulator/looping function.
E02 provides proximity, and E18 provides context, but there is no evidence of CTCF-dependent looping or regulatory interaction between the locus and MYC.
The chain explicitly requires CTCF occupancy in colorectal cancer cells (HCT116), which is not present in the provided ENCODE data (E04, E07).
This is highly speculative, relying only on general knowledge of chromatin architecture (E18) without specific evidence linking this variant's CTCF activity to the CRC phenotype.

grades_final.reason: TCF7L2 occupancy at the element in HCT116 is supported by ChIP peaks (E04, E05, E19), but no QBiC-SELEX or allele-specific binding data establish that the alt C allele binds more strongly. The direction is an untested inference, so the binding link is indirect/weak.
E01 and E03 directly place the variant in an active proximal enhancer-like cCRE (EH38E3858447) with DNase and H3K27ac signal consistent with a regulatory element. This supports the element claim.

E02 only shows MYC is 334.2 kb away. E18 is general CRC literature and E21 shows MYC is common-essential in HCT116, not that this enhancer specifically regulates MYC. No enhancer-promoter or perturbation evidence links EH38E3858447 to MYC.
E04 and E05 show TCF7L2 occupancy at this element in HCT116 and TCF7L2 expression in HCT116, supporting HCT116 as a relevant cell type for the proposed TCF7L2 mechanism.

The phenotype link rests on general CRC literature and MYC essentiality, not on variant-specific or CRC genetic evidence for this SNP. The credible sets in E16 are for PSA and urinary incontinence, not colorectal cancer, and E15 reports no GWAS association.

SP1 occupancy at the element in HCT116 is supported by ChIP peaks (E04, E06), but no QBiC-SELEX or allele-specific binding data show that the alt C allele binds SP1 more strongly. The direction is an untested inference, so the binding link is weak.

E01 and E03 directly place the variant in an active proximal enhancer-like cCRE (EH38E3858447) with DNase and H3K27ac signal. This supports the element claim, although SP1 responsiveness itself is not directly assayed.

E02 only gives distance to POU5F1B. E16 provides L2G support for POU5F1B in PSA and urinary incontinence credible sets, not colorectal cancer, and E17 reports no significant GTEx eQTL. No evidence links this enhancer to POU5F1B in HCT116 or CRC.
E04 and E06 show SP1 occupancy at this element in HCT116 and SP1 expression in HCT116, supporting HCT116 as a relevant cell type for the proposed SP1 mechanism.

E18 provides general literature support for POU5F1B in colorectal cancer, but there is no variant-specific, allele-specific, or enhancer-specific evidence tying this SNP and SP1 binding to a colorectal cancer phenotype.

checks.why: Verifies TCF7L2 occupancy and provides the basis for required ChIP data, although it will not resolve the directional allelic change.
This is the single most critical check to resolve the major flaw in H3: confirming whether CTCF actually binds this locus in the required cell type.
Although expression is cited in E05, a direct query confirms the expression data and associated context, ensuring the TF context is robustly defined for the cell-type claim.

next_experiment: Allele-specific enhancer reporter with T vs C in HCT116; low cost; H1 predicts a reproducible allelic activity difference while H4 predicts none. This is the cheapest experiment that separates the current top two chains H1 and H4.
